meta.title: Dead Air on the Meridian
meta.setting: The Meridian Limited, Train No. 7 westbound, Great Meridian Railway (fictional). Stopped by a snow slide at milepost 212 below Kestrel Pass, the night of Saturday 19 to Sunday 20 December 1936. Art Deco sleeper consist: baggage, Bellflower, Mesquite (diner), Larkspur (six drawing rooms), Juniper (club), Sundown (observation). All times are Pacific railroad time.
meta.ip_notes: Original characters, names and plot. Generic closed-circle conventions only (17 U.S.C. 102(b)). Distanced from Murder on the Orient Express (1934): no bolt business, no burnt-paper fragment (the telegram is flushed onto the snow instead), no kimono (Celeste wears a travelling coat), no stopped watch on the body, a one-night stop freed by a plow rather than days snowbound, one killer rather than a group, motive is exposure rather than revenge. Not the Roger Ackroyd trick: the exposing letter is a money demand, not a confession naming the blackmailer. Ellery Queen's phrase is never used; the gate is 'Briggs's Gate'. Railway and place names are invented; check them against real trademarks before any on-screen map.
meta.content_rating: Teen: implied violence (one off-screen blow), adult secrets (bigamy, blackmail, a fatal drunk operation, a stowaway minor), no gore, no drug content.

public.summary: America's most feared radio gossip, host of Crane's Corner. Found beaten to death in DR3.
public_facts: Hosts the Sunday-night program Crane's Corner and writes a syndicated column.
Signs off with 'This is Desmond Crane, and I hear everything.'
Travelling to broadcast Sunday's program live from San Francisco.
Carried a heavy chrome ribbon microphone in a fitted case and declaimed into it unplugged.
At dinner he said Sunday's broadcast would end a career on this very train.
Asked Briggs to wake him the moment there was word on the line.

secret.summary: Never typed a word; dictated to Nora. Tonight Celeste tried to pay him blackmail he never asked for; he recognised his own files and Nora's broken e, pencilled a telegram to the Oakland police, and confronted Nora at about 12:20. He bluffed that Miss Varga had the letter. Nora killed him at 12:25.

voice.design_instruction: A 1930s American radio gossip broadcaster, fast polished tenor, theatrical, sly.

public.summary: Crane's secretary for four years. Quiet, precise, faintly warm, holding her grief in tight. She hands you Crane's black notebook.

mannerisms: Answers every question fully and helpfully

secret.summary: She has run a blackmail racket in Crane's name for two years, copying items from his files and mailing typed letters signed 'A Friend of Mr. Crane's' to Box 1129, Chicago, on her portable with a cracked lowercase e. Crane found out tonight and was going to have her detained at Oakland. At 12:25 she struck him with his microphone, wiped it with a DR4 towel, flushed the torn telegram and threw the towel out of her window at 12:33. Her alibi rests on the Colonel's watch, which is on Denver time; she really sat with him from 10:58 to 11:40. Her Reno divorce is a real but innocent secret.

voice.design_instruction: A composed American woman, late twenties, soft clear mezzo, precise diction of a 1930s private secretary, warm but reserved, very even pace.

whereabouts.truth: In DR4 since 11:40 pm (aft in Sundown with the Colonel from 10:58 to 11:40 pm).
Called in by Crane about 12:20; strikes him at 12:25.
Tears and flushes the telegram, washes, throws the towel out at 12:33, shuts the window 12:35.

At 11:45 she went to DR3 to pay; Crane said he had never written to her, kept the letter and said someone was using his name. Left 11:55, losing an ear-clip. Teddy joined her in DR2 at 12:00; at 12:25 they heard a man's raised voice, someone answering low and level, a thump.

secret.summary: He was Sergeant Hargreave, Corps of Engineers, and promoted himself in 1919. His wife Martha died in Denver in 1931 and since then his pocket watch has stayed on Denver (Mountain) time, an hour ahead of the railroad. Every time he gives is honest and an hour fast: Nora really joined him at 10:58 and left at 11:40; the shutter came down at midnight; he reached DR6 at 12:02.

Finds the body at 1:35; with the Agent from 1:55.

public_facts: Sixteen, from Oklahoma.
Her family lost their farm.
Going to her aunt in Fresno.

cards.title: Crane's body
cards.description: Desmond Crane on the floor of DR3. One blow to the left temple.

cards.title: The wound pattern
cards.description: Dr. Ashcombe: a single blow to the left temple. The wound carries a fine crosshatch, 'like a sieve, or a grille.'

cards.title: The ribbon microphone
cards.description: Crane's heavy chrome ribbon microphone, latched in its fitted case on the rack. The grille is dented. It is spotless, when everything else Crane owned is smeared with fingerprints.

cards.title: A white thread in the grille
cards.description: A single white thread caught in the microphone grille. It looks like the doctor's cotton wool.
cards.herring_resolution: It points at Ashcombe's cotton wool, but once his own lie is broken he identifies it as spun, woven thread, which matches a railway huck towel, not loose wool.

cards.title: Ice bucket and soda
cards.description: A nickel ice bucket with a few slivers left, and a poured soda, untouched. He died soon after the ice came.

cards.title: The telegraph pad
cards.description: A Meridian Line Telegram pad. The top sheet is torn off. In raking light the next sheet shows faint pressure marks.

cards.title: The rubbed telegraph pad
cards.description: Pencil rubbing of the pad: 'CHIEF OF POLICE OAKLAND -- MEET NO 7 OAKLAND PIER STOP HAVE PROOF OF BLACKMAIL--'. The second line is too faint to read. On its own, it reads as Crane being blackmailed.

cards.title: The typed letter to Miss Varga
cards.description: A typed letter to 'Miss Varga', dated December 10, demanding $2,000 'before Christmas' to Post Office Box 1129, Chicago. Signed 'A Friend of Mr. Crane's.' The lowercase e prints with a gap at the top. Found in the inside pocket of Crane's jacket.

cards.title: Sunday's script, in longhand
cards.description: Crane's draft of Sunday's broadcast, every word in his own longhand pencil.

cards.title: Crane's black notebook
cards.description: Longhand entries on everyone aboard: 'VARGA -- & the dancing boy (Lowell, Newark).' 'ASHCOMBE -- Vandermeer. SUNDAY (tick).' 'HARGREAVE -- "Colonel"?? War Dept. reply pending.' 'PELL -- the Reno business (33). Keep her grateful.' The manifest is ticked in pencil.
cards.herring_resolution: Every entry is a real secret, which makes everyone look like a suspect. Only one secret is murder; 'PELL -- Reno' is an innocent divorce.

cards.title: The DR2 connecting door
cards.description: The connecting door between DR2 and DR3, bolted on Crane's side.
cards.herring_resolution: Neutral: it tells you nothing about who came in. Celeste used the corridor door at 11:45 and left at 11:55.

cards.title: A diamond ear-clip
cards.description: A diamond ear-clip under Crane's seat.
cards.herring_resolution: Celeste was in DR3, but she left at 11:55. Ellis delivered ice at 12:10 and Crane was alive (E-BUCKET, T-ELL-ICE).

cards.title: The flushing plate
cards.description: Brass plate: 'Passengers will kindly refrain from flushing while the train is standing.' The toilet empties onto the track.

cards.title: The engine and train log
cards.description: '11:05 PT stopped MP 212.' Briggs forward to the slide 11:08, back 1:30.

cards.title: The dining-car menu card
cards.description: 'Pacific Standard Time is observed west of Cinder Junction. Kindly set your watches back one hour.'

cards.title: The Colonel's pocket watch
cards.description: Martha's gift. It reads exactly one hour ahead of Briggs's railroad-standard watch: still on Denver (Mountain) time.

cards.title: The club-car notice
cards.description: Brass notice over the Juniper bar: 'This car closes at midnight.' The shutter came down at 12:00.

cards.title: The passenger manifest
cards.description: No Morton or Norton aboard. 'E. Lowell' holds upper berth 9 in Bellflower, a cheap berth for a Boston heir.

cards.title: A 1918 photograph
cards.description: Hargreave in uniform, 1918. Zoomed in: sergeant's chevrons.

cards.title: An old service revolver
cards.description: Dusty and unfired, at the bottom of the Colonel's valise.
cards.herring_resolution: Nobody was shot. Crane died of one blow from a grille-faced object.

cards.title: Blood on the doctor's cuff
cards.description: A smear of blood on Dr. Ashcombe's right cuff.
cards.herring_resolution: From his examination of the body at 1:50, which he explains at once and truthfully.

cards.title: Celeste's travel clock
cards.description: Set to Pacific time, a studio habit. It backs up her and Teddy's 12:25.

cards.title: Two brands in the ashtray
cards.description: Two brands of cigarette ends in DR2's ashtray. She wasn't alone.

cards.title: The shoes, chalked and dull
cards.description: Briggs: the shoes in the smoking room were 'sitting there chalked and dull' when he came through at 1:35.

cards.title: Nora's wristwatch
cards.description: Nora's wristwatch, lying on her typewriter in DR4.

cards.title: Nora's portable typewriter
cards.description: A test line on Nora's portable reproduces the cracked lowercase e, gapped at the top.

cards.title: Typed fair copies
cards.description: Fair copies of Crane's scripts from Nora's dictation folder. Every lowercase e is gapped at the top.

cards.title: One towel in DR4
cards.description: DR4's rail holds one huck towel. Every other drawing room has two.

cards.title: A stained towel in the snow
cards.description: A pink-stained huck towel, 'GREAT MERIDIAN' woven in, half under the snow directly below DR4. DR3's window is latched from inside.

cards.title: Telegram scraps in the snow
cards.description: Wet scraps of a Meridian Line Telegram blank on the snow under DR4. One reads '--BY ONE IN MY EMPL--'.

cards.title: Small bootprints
cards.description: Small bootprints on the far side, running from the baggage car toward the slide.
cards.herring_resolution: Dottie Hale climbed down at 11:30 to look at the slide. The prints run along the far side toward the engine, never under Larkspur's windows.

cards.title: Crane at dinner
cards.description: 'Sunday's broadcast will end a career on this very train.' He also asked the Colonel 'Which regiment was that?' and the Colonel said 'I don't fiddle my watch for any railroad, sir.'

cards.title: "He'd never written to me"
cards.description: Celeste went to DR3 at 11:45 to pay $2,000. Crane: 'Madam, I have never written you a letter in my life.' He read it, went white, kept it, and said 'Someone has been using my name.' She left at 11:55.

cards.title: The thump at 12:25
cards.description: Through the connecting door, by Celeste's travel clock: a man's raised voice, someone answering low and level, then a heavy thump. 'Nobody was crying.'

cards.title: Ruth Kowalczyk
cards.description: Celeste Varga is Ruth Kowalczyk of Braddock, Pennsylvania. She married a mill hand at seventeen and never divorced him.

cards.title: Teddy in DR2
cards.description: Teddy left the club car at 11:58 and was in DR2 with Celeste from 12:00 to 12:45.

cards.title: Edward Lowell of Newark
cards.description: Teddy is Edward Lowell, a dance-hall instructor from Newark. Same name as the Boston Lowells, different class.

cards.title: "The e's were broken"
cards.description: Ashcombe has paid $500 a month to Box 1129 for fourteen months. 'The letters were typed. A poor machine. The e's were broken.'

cards.title: Water in DR4 at 12:30
cards.description: Ashcombe, awake with his lamp on: ice next door but one at 12:10; a knock and Crane's raised voice about 12:20; at 12:30 by his watch, water running in DR4 for several minutes and the toilet flushing; about 12:33, a cold draught along the floor.

cards.title: "That's spun thread"
cards.description: Ashcombe: 'That's spun thread, Agent, woven stuff. My wool is loose fluff. Compare it with a railway towel.'
keywords: compare it with a railway towel

cards.title: Sergeant Hargreave
cards.description: Hargreave was a sergeant in the Corps of Engineers and promoted himself in 1919. 'Don't tell my daughter.'

cards.title: "It's her time"
cards.description: Martha is buried in Denver. Since 1931 the Colonel has kept his watch on Denver time. Every time he has given is an hour fast: Nora was with him from 10:58 to 11:40, not midnight to 12:40.

cards.title: "He never touched a typewriter"
cards.description: Nora: 'He never touched a typewriter in his life. He called it women's work.'

cards.title: Ice at 12:10
cards.description: Ellis: DR3 rang at 12:05; ice and soda at 12:10. Crane was shaking, writing on a telegraph pad. 'Any wires, sir?' 'Not yet. Don't disturb me again tonight.'

cards.title: Two towels a room
cards.description: Ellis: 'Two towels every room, every night.'

cards.title: "Mr. Crane never typed"
cards.description: Ellis: 'Mr. Crane never typed, sir. Called it women's work.'

cards.title: The doctor's lamp
cards.description: Ellis: 'Doctor's reading lamp was on under his door all night.'

cards.title: Light under the doctor's door
cards.description: Briggs: 'Doctor's light was on under his door when I came through at 1:35.'

cards.title: Steward Fisk's statement
cards.description: Via Briggs: Fisk was in the diner galley 11:10-11:50 making crew coffee. Saw Miss Pell go aft about eleven. Mr. Lowell was the last one out at 11:58. Shutter down at midnight; the Colonel came through just as he pulled it.

cards.title: Teddy saw Nora
cards.description: Teddy: Nora went aft about eleven and came forward about twenty to twelve. 'I'd had a few, don't hold me to it.'

cards.title: Dottie in the baggage car
cards.description: Ellis has hidden his sister's girl, Dottie Hale, 16, in the baggage car since Ogden. He was with her 12:15-12:35, not shining shoes.
cards.herring_resolution: Explains Ellis's absence during the murder window and his shoe lie. It costs him something to give.

cards.title: Miss Varga at 11:55
cards.description: Ellis: at 11:55 Miss Varga was in the corridor, coat over her nightdress, coming from the direction of DR3.

cards.title: Mr. Lowell at midnight
cards.description: Ellis: at 12:00 Mr. Lowell slipped into DR2.

cards.title: The Colonel to bed at 12:02
cards.description: Ellis: the Colonel came in from the club car to DR6 at 12:02. 'While I was at my seat, Miss Pell never went aft. And nobody came forward from that club car at twenty to one.'

cards.title: A window at 12:35
cards.description: Ellis: coming back at 12:35 he heard a window bang shut somewhere mid-car and felt cold along the floor.

cards.title: Mr. Lowell at 12:45
cards.description: Ellis: at 12:45 Mr. Lowell went forward.

cards.title: Dottie's account
cards.description: Dottie: Uncle Ellis was with her from 12:15 to 12:35 with a blanket and sandwiches. She climbed down at 11:30 on the far side to look at the slide; those are her bootprints.

cards.title: The flagman
cards.description: 'Saw the old gent and the secretary lady in Sundown when I went out the back. Right after we stopped. Eleven-oh-six by my watch.'

cards.title: Nora's alibi
cards.description: Nora: 'I went aft about midnight. The Colonel and I sat until twenty to one. Then I went to bed.'

cards.title: Nora on the stop
cards.description: Nora: 'We stopped just after I sat down, around midnight. I nearly fell. The Colonel caught my arm.'

cards.title: "He used my machine"
cards.description: Nora, shown the broken e: 'Mr. Crane used my machine whenever he liked.'

cards.title: The Colonel's shutter
cards.description: The Colonel: 'The steward was pulling down his shutter as I came through. One o'clock. I turned in.'

cards.title: C-STOP: the stop was at 11:05
cards.description: Nora says the train stopped just after she sat down, 'around midnight'. The log (or the flagman) puts the stop at 11:05. She was in Sundown at 11:05. A stepping stone, not proof.

cards.title: C-LONGHAND: a longhand man
cards.description: The blackmail letter is typed. Crane wrote everything in longhand and never typed. Someone else wrote it.

cards.title: C-DENVER: the Denver time
cards.description: The Colonel's watch runs an hour fast (Denver time). Nora's 'with the Colonel till twenty to one' was really till twenty to twelve.

cards.title: C-SHUTTER: one o'clock was midnight
cards.description: The Colonel says the shutter came down 'at one o'clock' as he came through. The notice and the steward say midnight. His clock is an hour fast, and so is Nora's alibi.

cards.title: C-BEDTIME: the Colonel was in bed
cards.description: Ellis saw the Colonel go to DR6 at 12:02. Nobody came forward from the club car at 12:40, and Nora never went aft while he was at his seat. She can't have sat with the Colonel till 12:40.

cards.title: C-TELEGRAM: one in my employ
cards.description: Pad and scraps together: 'CHIEF OF POLICE OAKLAND -- MEET NO 7 OAKLAND PIER STOP HAVE PROOF OF BLACKMAIL BY ONE IN MY EMPLOY STOP DETAIN--'. Crane was exposing the blackmailer, someone he employed, and it was flushed from DR4.

cards.title: C-TYPE: he never typed
cards.description: Nora: 'He never touched a typewriter in his life.' Then, shown the broken e: 'Mr. Crane used my machine whenever he liked.' Both can't be true.

cards.title: C-BROKEN-E: the same broken e
cards.description: The blackmail letter and Nora's machine print the same cracked lowercase e. The letters were typed on her typewriter.

cards.title: C-TOWEL: the missing towel
cards.description: DR4 is one towel short. A pink-stained GREAT MERIDIAN towel lies in the snow directly below DR4.

cards.title: C-FIBRE: thread from a towel
cards.description: The thread in the microphone grille is spun, woven thread, not the doctor's wool. It matches the stained towel thrown from DR4.

cards.title: C-WATER: water in an empty room
cards.description: At 12:30 Ashcombe heard water run and the toilet flush in DR4, while Nora claims she was in Sundown until 12:40.

claims.speaker: CH-NOR

claims.note: True on the Colonel's clock; false in railroad time (the stop was 11:05).

claims.speaker: CH-NOR
claims.text: I heard nothing from Mr. Crane's room after dictation.

claims.speaker: CH-NOR
claims.text: Mr. Crane used my machine whenever he liked.
claims.note: Contradicts her own 'He never touched a typewriter in his life' (T-NEVERTYPED).

claims.speaker: CH-NOR
claims.text: I never saw what he was writing.

claims.speaker: CH-NOR
claims.text: The porter must have left me only the one towel.
claims.note: Added in transcription so the physical lock has a claim to crack. Ellis: two every room, every night.

claims.speaker: CH-NOR
claims.text: I've never seen that letter before, Agent. 'A Friend of Mr. Crane's' means nothing to me.
claims.note: Added in transcription: she typed it. Broken by C-BROKEN-E.

claims.speaker: CH-CEL
claims.text: I went to bed at eleven and never left my compartment.

claims.speaker: CH-CEL
claims.note: Teddy was in DR2 from 12:00 to 12:45.

claims.speaker: CH-CEL
claims.text: I am the Countess Celeste Varga, of Budapest.

claims.speaker: CH-TED
claims.text: I played cards in the club car till one, with a salesman from Bellflower. Morton. Or Norton.
claims.note: The car closed at midnight; he was last out at 11:58; no Morton or Norton on the manifest.

claims.speaker: CH-TED
claims.note: Edward Lowell of Newark: same name, different class.

claims.speaker: CH-ASH
claims.text: I never had any dealings with Crane.
